$comment: Hash of each frozen version's slice in the dump it was blessed from, excluding doc/description/examples (none of which reach the generated output), taken off the parsed dump before generation runs (see lib/dump-digest.mts). Generation fails if a frozen version's slice moves, because its files are skipped and the rest of the tree would be generated against a model they no longer hold. Run `yarn generate:api` and paste what it prints to seed a version. Record $source when you do.
$source: ghcr.io/truenas/middleware:master, middlewared 20261103085853~truenas+1 (digest sha256:78886a229fb3ea0aad1d88f54a070c5bb613a2599b31a1b75af0d207b5995887, fetched 2026-11-03). Everything the 2026-10-05 seed recorded still holds and is not repeated here; what follows is what moved. Eight slices still, and no renumbering this time. **This is the first seed where leaving the frozen files alone was the wrong answer.** The dump now reports app.available, app.latest, nvmet.global.sessions, reporting.graphs and reporting.netdata_graphs at every slice, where the 2026-10-05 dump reported them only at v28.0.0. They are not a leak: api/v25_10_0/reporting.py and app.py have modelled ReportingGraphsItem, AppAvailableItem and AppLatestItem since 25.10's API was introduced, and middleware's 6113c3b872 ('Properly handle filterable methods versioned API') fixed filterable methods being mis-registered for versioned APIs -- with a test asserting every filterable method is callable. The dump was wrong about 25.10 before and is right now. Reseeding alone would therefore have deleted all five from the whole tree, v28 included, where they work today: the generator computes them as inherited from 25.10 and leaves them out of the later deltas, and the frozen file did not declare them. That is the gate's own warning -- 'later versions may reference entries the frozen files lack' -- firing for real, and it was measured by regenerating into a copy of the tree with the markers in place, not predicted. So the five calls and their nine types are hand-added to v25_10_0 (each patch index re-exports the names, since a patch re-exports from the root rather than from its predecessor), and v27.0.0 and v28.0.0 inherit them. Verified with the compiler at all three versions, and all five are chain-stable enough to join ApiCallDirectoryBase. The frozen files are still not regenerated, because the rest of the 25.10 drift is the usual leak and would come with it: seven event payloads moved -- cloud_backup.query, cloudsync.query, container.query, rsynctask.query, sharing.s3.query, sharing.webshare.query and vm.query -- carrying master's models into a released version's types. Hand-adding takes the five without taking those. Two 25.10 changes reach no type. The removed_in renumber landed (aervin, upstream): the values now read v27/v28 where they read v26/v27, which is eleven of the twelve changed 25.10 methods. The twelfth is group.query, and it moved only because its doc went from a string to null -- dumpDigest strips doc when it is a string, so a *removed* docstring still drifts a hash the digest is meant to ignore. Worth fixing in the digest rather than here. At v28.0.0: ContainerEntry.status becomes nullable, middleware's own description saying 'null if query-options.extra.retrieve_status is false', so v28 re-declares an entry v27 had and the two clients' container mapping genuinely diverges. Ten entries also leave ApiCallDirectoryBase -- auth.me, auth.twofactor.update, filesystem.stat, group.get_group_obj, nfs.update, replication.count_eligible_manual_snapshots, user.get_user_obj, user.set_password, user.shell_choices and user.unset_2fa_secret -- each because its model was renamed or extracted at v28 (UserSetPasswordArgs became UserSetPassword; AuthMeResult.privilege became a $ref to a new ComposedPrivilege). All ten changed at v28.0.0 only, so the eviction is correct and the names are part of the surface; an unversioned caller has to name a version for those.
